title: Bank Deposit Transfers Held Side by Side: Each Booking Stands Alone
content:
A customer may hold any number of Bank Deposit transfers at once. Every booking is its own transfer, with its own confirmation number, principal, fees, locked exchange rate and disclosed date of availability.

## The rule

1. **No count limit.** There is no cap on how many Bank Deposit transfers one customer may hold at the same time. What bounds them is the aggregate sending limits of the customer's Personal Sender Account and the per-recipient frequency cap of Bank Deposit.
2. **No merging.** Transfers are never merged, netted or batched.
3. **Each on its own.** Each transfer is priced, cancelled, refunded, returned and resolved on its own.
4. **No offsetting.** A refund or a fee refund on one transfer never offsets an amount on another transfer.

## Questions the rule answers

**Is there a maximum number of open Bank Deposit transfers per customer?**
No. The number is unlimited; only the sending limits of the Personal Sender Account and the per-recipient frequency cap bound new bookings.

**Two transfers to the same recipient were booked on the same day. Are their fees worked out together?**
No. Each is priced on its own principal under its own tier, exactly as if the other did not exist.

**A fee is being refunded on one transfer while the customer owes nothing on another. Can the refund be applied to the other transfer?**
No. A refund or fee refund belongs to the transfer it arose on and never offsets an amount on another.

*Hypothetical illustration:* a customer holds three Bank Deposit transfers, one deposited, one in transit and one awaiting funds. A cancellation of the transfer awaiting funds refunds only what was collected on that transfer; the other two keep their own fees, rates and dates unchanged.
